audit_scope: Historical evidence, direct 2015 Hill Country vegetative PDF pages, staging Diggs reproductive dossiers, modern nomenclature and supplemental public sources. No new Hays source photo pixels opened.
method_limits: Eight stored source observation sets and earlier photo QA were read; earlier reviewed-photo counts are NOT new visual inspections.
Direct attempt to open specific iNaturalist photo and observation pages did not return pixels in this run. No photo can be signed off from page metadata or iNaturalist research grade.
Public comparison photographs from other places cannot identify specific Hays individuals.
The regional-flora reproductive details in prepared packets were reviewed, not re-opened against the private source PDF in this batch.
Hagenbuch & Lemke (2015) printed p.54 and p.67 were visually checked on the original public PDF using page screenshots.
Photo-license fields are historical preflight data, not currently approved rights. No image published, no manifests/key states changed.

records.previous_source_photo_visible_notes: Loose panicle branches with pendulous pale spikelets, leaf blades and tussock context; some hand-scaled flowering heads.
records.previous_source_photo_unresolved_notes: Fertile-floret count and sterile-rudiment shape not resolved; glume inequality and inner ligule dimensions not measurable.
regional_and_external_sources: Hagenbuch & Lemke 2015 p.54, verified directly: perennial cespitose; rhizomes and stolons absent, though hard subrhizomatous base; sheaths almost closed; decurrent membranous ligule 3–6 mm.
Diggs et al. 1999 printed p.1284 (packet 1): terminal sterile rudiments and floret number distinguish Melica mutica.
records.new_evidence_reconciliation: CONFLICT: packet 1 says rhizomatous perennial; 2015 primary vegetative account explicitly says rhizomes and stolons absent. Do not equate a subrhizomatous hard base with demonstrated true rhizomes.
records.exact_remaining_specimen_evidence: From one Hays collected or documented plant: rooted basal crown, entire sheath-throat/ligule with millimeter scale, one mature dissected spikelet exposing 2–3 fertile florets and terminal sterile rudiments. Compare M. mutica.
records.local_context_blocker: Dingee 89 (SWT), explicitly listed under Hays County in 2015 appendix; this verifies prior local occurrence reference, not the current iNaturalist species ID.
records.rights_blocker: No directly permissive photo among saved iNaturalist sample; NC-only preflight.

records.previous_source_photo_visible_notes: Very narrow pencil-like cylindrical inflorescence with obvious successive nodes/segment pattern and hand scale; erect to arching culms and natural grassy habitat in several independent observations.
records.previous_source_photo_unresolved_notes: Sessile spikelet rachis-niche architecture, pitted glume and exact membrane ligule cannot be resolved in photographs; confirm with dissection before final species-ID signoff.
regional_and_external_sources: Diggs et al. 1999 printed p.1258 under Coelorachis cylindrica (packet 1): jointed slender cylindrical raceme with rachis niches and pitted sessile glume.
POWO 2026 currently accepts Rottboellia campestris and lists Coelorachis cylindrica as heterotypic synonym; GrassBase/FNA had other genus usage.
records.new_evidence_reconciliation: NAME-LINK: staged candidate taxonomy_url points to POWO Coelorachis cylindrica synonym landing page (62724-2), not accepted Rottboellia campestris page (419621-1). Keep historical synonym for search; do not substitute Coelorachis traits from unrelated taxa.
records.exact_remaining_specimen_evidence: Same Hays source plant: sharply focused 1-mm-scale rachis joint in which sessile spikelet sits in its niche, pitted outer glume, disarticulated joint and basal ligule. Compare other jointed Andropogoneae.
records.local_context_blocker: Published Hays collections Carr 10681 and Sanders 4100 (TEX-LL) cited in staging; original sheet micromorphology not rechecked.
records.rights_blocker: One historic CC0 source-photo metadata candidate, photo 684707043; current photo license/access and same-specimen detail not rechecked.

records.previous_source_photo_visible_notes: Several slender racemes on branched flowering stalks, paired rows of spikelets in macro view, strap-like basal leaves, wooded/rocky ground context in some observations.
records.previous_source_photo_unresolved_notes: First-glume presence and dark brown glandular blotches on second glume/sterile lemma cannot be verified at this review scale; species identification unproven.
regional_and_external_sources: Diggs et al. 1999 printed p.1306, packet 1: paired spikelets and variable first/lower glume; critical glandular/pubescent details.
POWO/GrassBase current treatment says tufted perennial with 2–5 racemes; Faccenda 2023 Bishop Museum paper describes annual habit and usually 1–3 racemes in Hawaiian plants.
records.new_evidence_reconciliation: SOURCE-CONFLICT: the 2023 Paspalum langei account (Hawaiian records) differs from POWO/GrassBase on life history and typical raceme count. Do not make annual/perennial or 2 vs. 3 racemes a hard filter without taxon-concept/regional reconciliation.
records.exact_remaining_specimen_evidence: Revisit original Hays TEX00568499, TEX00568501 and TEX00485588 at 1-mm scale, resolve first glume on each paired spikelet, glume glandular spots and hairs; match a current Hays source plant. Check the possible planted 2019 yard specimen separately.
records.local_context_blocker: Three original TEX sheets previously inspected but microscopic determinations not independently confirmed; 23 Hays iNat observations are not verified specimens.
records.rights_blocker: Two CC BY historical iNaturalist photo metadata candidates by Noland Martin; license and pixel/diagnostic roles need current verification.

records.previous_source_photo_visible_notes: Bottlebrush-like narrow fuzzy panicles, often green but some tan, and visible radiating bristles, clumped annual-looking plants.
records.previous_source_photo_unresolved_notes: Short-burst bristle arrangement and finely rugose fertile lemma are not resolved against Setaria pumila, S. parviflora and other foxtails; many closeup images of head but no spikelet dissections.
regional_and_external_sources: Hagenbuch & Lemke 2015: annual; ligule fringe of hairs, base/sheath traits in staging crosswalk.
Diggs et al. 1999 printed p.1320 (packet 1): flowering spikelets and finely rugose mature fertile lemma.
FNA Setaria account and idtools comparative key: S. viridis has relatively few subtending bristles (often 1–3), while S. pumila often 4–12; overlap and photo framing require actual spikelet views.
records.new_evidence_reconciliation: The green fuzzy head is genus-level support only. Add mandatory leaf-collar / basal rooting / mature fertile lemma / bristle-group evidence before this is a species endpoint; avoid using just green bristle color.
records.exact_remaining_specimen_evidence: One mature Hays plant photographed from rooted annual base through collar to inflorescence, with separated spikelet, counted bristles and finely wrinkled fertile lemma at scale; compare S. pumila and S. parviflora.
records.local_context_blocker: Published Hays SWT gatherings Liang 50, Osborn 35 referenced; distinct from unapproved iNaturalist image specimens.
records.rights_blocker: Two CC BY iNaturalist photo metadata candidates; current licenses not independently rechecked.

records.previous_source_photo_visible_notes: Small tufted/stolonlike grass and short branched, sometimes crowded panicle with small spikelets; one wet-soil observation.
records.previous_source_photo_unresolved_notes: Panicle architecture and glume/lemma hair/awn details do not conclusively separate E. colona from other Echinochloa and lookalike Paniceae.
regional_and_external_sources: Hagenbuch & Lemke 2015 leaf-collar context (staging crosswalk): no ligule; purple bands can vary.
Diggs et al. 1999 printed p.1266 packet 2: mature spikelet/glume/lemma separation from other Echinochloa.
records.new_evidence_reconciliation: Hays historical photos show probable Echinochloa architecture, not a species-level exclusion of E. walteri or E. crus-galli. Purple leaf V's are not reliable alone. Keep GBIF false-fuzzy Echinochloa colonum alias rejected.
records.exact_remaining_specimen_evidence: Same rooted Hays individual: leaf collar proving ligule absence plus multiple mature spikelets viewed dorsally and in profile at mm scale; document awn and sterile lemma surface, compare E. walteri and E. crus-galli.
records.local_context_blocker: Breckenridge 441 (SWT) historic Hays voucher citation, but no specimen correspondence to current photos.
records.rights_blocker: Hays historical iNaturalist samples NC-only; comparative Commons galleries elsewhere do not validate Hays specimen.

records.previous_source_photo_visible_notes: Exceptionally useful Hays photos: small tuft, long narrow panicles, scaly overlapping spikelets, partial collar/ligule, mature branches in hand.
records.previous_source_photo_unresolved_notes: Species boundary versus Tridentopsis mutica and T. buckleyana depends on lemma/callus, florets, ligule and anther dimensions not all reliably measured.
regional_and_external_sources: Diggs et al. 1999 printed p.1330 under Tridens muticus var. elongatus, packet 1: typically broader blade and more-veined second glume relative to var. muticus.
POWO 2026 accepts Tridentopsis elongata as a distinct species and lists Tridens muticus var. elongatus as synonym.
records.new_evidence_reconciliation: Name currently resolved, but old broad muticus taxon labels cannot be used as independent species proof. GBIF Trisetopsis elongata is a false fuzzy match and must not be adopted.
records.exact_remaining_specimen_evidence: From single Hays plant: measure blade width, photograph one flattened illuminated upper glume to count 3–7 nerves and verify size, with other spikelets, lemma/callus traits and a 1-mm ruler; compare T. mutica and T. buckleyana.
records.local_context_blocker: Three Hays photo observations, only two historical observers; no cited Hays physical voucher.
records.rights_blocker: Five CC BY saved photo metadata candidates by Eric Knight; no fresh source-photo pixel/license reinspection.

records.previous_source_photo_visible_notes: Slender interrupted-looking spikes with close-up overlapping green spikelets and sheath/stem junction views.
records.previous_source_photo_unresolved_notes: Second glume shape, ligule and floret details not decisively visible; compare existing Sphenopholis obtusata candidate.
regional_and_external_sources: Hagenbuch & Lemke 2015 p.67 describes this under synonym Trisetum interruptum: annual cespitose, no rhizomes/stolons; hairy leaf sheaths; 1–2 mm membranous ligule; narrow leaves.
ITIS currently links Trisetum interruptum Buckley as synonym of Sphenopholis interrupta.
Earlier staging requests glume, floret and ligule dissection against S. obtusata; no direct new Hays specimen measurements.
records.new_evidence_reconciliation: PRIMARY-SOURCE CROSSWALK: 2015 Hill Country vegetative account is present as Trisetum interruptum; it should be linked to the Sphenopholis interrupta dossier instead of appearing as unavailable. The vegetative character set does NOT by itself establish the species in source photographs.
records.exact_remaining_specimen_evidence: One Hays flowering individual: 1–2 mm ligule, hispid sheath, mature spikelet showing upper glume shape, awn and floret details; matched comparison against S. obtusata, not head outline alone.
records.local_context_blocker: Three historical Hays observations; no independently examined Hays voucher.
records.rights_blocker: Four CC BY saved source-photo metadata candidates by Eric Knight, still need current rights and pixel inspection.

records.previous_source_photo_visible_notes: Woody running bamboo thicket, narrow lanceolate leaves and node branching, multiple culms; compatible with Phyllostachys.
records.previous_source_photo_unresolved_notes: Basal culm internode crowding/compression characteristic of fishpole bamboo, grooved internodes and branch node details not demonstrated; planting or escaped-colony provenance not established.
regional_and_external_sources: Diggs et al. 1999 printed p.1311 (packet 7): species-specific basal culm and branching characters; flowering rare and must not be required.
records.new_evidence_reconciliation: Woody bamboo colony and foliage only support Phyllostachys; establish characteristic congested basal internodes and asymmetric node branches to support P. aurea, and distinguish planting or escape.
records.exact_remaining_specimen_evidence: Photograph measured lower culm internodes, nodal groove/flattening, unequal branches, sheath tip bristles from the same patch; obtain location/management or historical record proving planted, escaped or naturally reproducing.
records.local_context_blocker: Twelve Hays observations; probable planted/spreading colonies, no established wild-population proof.
records.rights_blocker: Three historic CC BY source-photo metadata candidates by Joseph Aubert; verification and site-license assessment pending.
